annotateddoc.title: The trial abstract, annotated
paragraphs: In this 68-week, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 1,961 adults with a body-mass index of 30 or greater to once-weekly semaglutide (2.4 mg) or placebo, plus lifestyle intervention.

The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was −14.9% in the semaglutide group, as compared with −2.4% with placebo. Participants who received semaglutide had greater improvements in cardiometabolic risk factors.
Nausea and diarrhea were the most common adverse events; they were typically transient and mild-to-moderate and subsided over time.

highlights.note: Large, adequately powered sample for a Phase 3 obesity RCT.

docview.title: The method paper, the scheme I used

blocks.text: We use a collocated finite-volume discretization with Rhie–Chow interpolation to suppress checkerboard pressure modes.
Stability requires the under-relaxation factors to satisfy α_p + α_u ≤ 1 on stretched meshes.
Outside this bound the continuity residual stalls rather than decays, the failure mode in run 043.

docview.note: This is the line your run 043 violated (you had α_u = 0.85). Run 044 sits exactly on the bound, which is why the residual finally decays instead of stalling.
docview.footer: I pulled the stability condition straight from the paper and tied it to why 043 stalled and 044 converged, no re-reading 22 pages.

researchsummary.title: GLP-1 agonists, evidence summary
researchsummary.question: Are GLP-1 receptor agonists effective and safe for long-term weight management in adults with obesity?
researchsummary.method: Cochrane systematic review + meta-analysis of 14 RCTs
findings: Semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved mean body-weight reduction of 12–15% vs 2–3% for placebo.
All GLP-1 agonists outperformed placebo on the primary weight outcome (high certainty).
Cardiovascular event rates fell significantly in high-risk populations (SELECT trial).
Gastrointestinal side-effects (nausea, vomiting) are common but typically transient.
researchsummary.conclusion: GLP-1 agonists are the most effective pharmacotherapy for obesity currently available. Long-term benefit requires continuous use, discontinuation leads to weight regain within one year.
researchsummary.limitations: Most trials exclude people with prior GI surgery; long-term safety beyond 5 years is not yet established.
researchsummary.source: Iepsen et al. · Cochrane Database Syst Rev · 2023

hypothesiscard.title: SELECT trial, primary hypothesis
hypothesiscard.h0: Semaglutide 2.4 mg does not reduce the rate of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and established cardiovascular disease, without diabetes.
hypothesiscard.h1: Semaglutide 2.4 mg reduces the rate of MACE versus placebo in this population.

variables.iv: Treatment arm, semaglutide 2.4 mg vs placebo
variables.dv: Time to first MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke)

hypothesiscard.footer: HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.72–0.90), p < 0.001 — a highly significant reduction in MACE.

casebrief.title: The precedent behind that redline
casebrief.facts: Bell signed a 24-month services agreement with a silent auto-renewal clause requiring 90 days notice to opt out. Bell missed the window by six days and was billed for a full renewal term it no longer wanted.
casebrief.issue: Whether a 90-day auto-renewal notice window, buried in a boilerplate term clause, is enforceable against a sophisticated commercial buyer who never separately negotiated it.
casebrief.holding: Enforceable, but only narrowly — the clause was conspicuously formatted and the buyer had counsel review the contract; the court signaled a shorter, negotiated window would likely have been required otherwise.
casebrief.reasoning: The court weighed three things: whether the term was buried or set apart, whether the buyer had a real chance to negotiate it, and whether 90 days exceeds commercial custom (it found market practice clusters at 30–60 days). All three cut close, so it upheld the clause narrowly rather than setting a bright-line rule.
casebrief.footer: The takeaway for §8.2: a 90-day window is defensible, but only barely, negotiating it down to 30 removes the risk entirely.

claimElements.text: receiving, at a server, a stream of shipment-location updates from a plurality of mobile devices
storing each location update in a distributed ledger replicated across at least three nodes
detecting a conflict between two location updates for the same shipment received within a threshold time window
automatically resolving the conflict using a timestamp-priority rule without human intervention

cells.quote: Edge devices stream GPS pings to the ingest cluster every 4 seconds.
Sensor readings are logged to a central event bus polled by field units.
Every update is written to a 3-node Raft-replicated ledger before ack.
Readings are mirrored to a backup store for durability.
Acme’s docs describe "duplicate suppression," which may or may not be the claimed conflict detection — worth a follow-up question.
Resolved coordinates post to the live tracking map within 400ms.

patentclaimchart.footer: Acme's platform is missing element 1.4 — conflicts get flagged for manual review, not auto-resolved — so it doesn't literally practice the claim; no license carve-out needed to sign. Same gap means this reference doesn't invalidate the patent either, so revisit if Acme ever ships auto-resolution.

storystructure.title: Draft: council approves bridge funding
storystructure.lede: The City Council voted 5-2 Tuesday night to approve $12 million in emergency funding for a new pedestrian bridge over Route 9, after two years of delay following a fatal crossing accident.
storystructure.nutGraf: The vote ends a contentious two-year debate that pitted residents demanding safer crossings against a council wary of the price tag. Construction is expected to begin next spring and finish by 2028, funded largely by a state safety grant secured last month.
body: Council member Elena Vasquez, who sponsored the funding measure, said the vote “finally puts safety ahead of cost” after years of near-misses at the intersection.
The bridge will connect the Riverside neighborhood to the transit hub on the north side of Route 9, a stretch pedestrians currently cross at grade despite a 45 mph speed limit.
Two council members who voted no, Raymond Chu and Priya Patel, said they support the bridge in principle but wanted a competitive bid process before locking in a contractor.
Construction is slated to begin in April, with the city's public works department targeting a completion date in late 2027.
background: The push for a bridge gained urgency after a cyclist was struck and killed at the intersection in March 2025, prompting a petition that collected more than 3,000 signatures.
The city considered a traffic-light-only fix in 2023 but shelved it after a traffic study found it would only reduce, not eliminate, the crossing risk.
The $12 million project includes an $8 million state Safe Streets grant awarded last month, with the remaining $4 million drawn from the city's capital reserve fund.
storystructure.footer: Inverted pyramid: the vote and its stakes lead, the who-said-what follows, history stays below the fold.
